A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PartCATSeg research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Their complete contents support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation experiments, cross-dataset evaluations, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix Tables A1–A3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original segmentation experiments, cross-dataset evaluations, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix Tables A1–A3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same cost aggregation, compositional loss, DINO guidance, and prediction procedures. Figure 4 revises the depicted DINO connections to match the existing spatial-aggregation description; this does not establish an underlying algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Pascal-Part-116, ADE20K-Part-234, PartImageNet, PartImageNet (OOD), and transfer from PartImageNet to Pascal-Part-116. Appendix F retains the same dataset coverage and class lists.

E2.justification: The experiment-specific comparator sets are unchanged in Tables 1–4 and A1–A2. ZSSeg+, VLPart, CLIPSeg, CAT-Seg, PartGLEE, and PartCLIPSeg remain in their respective comparisons, with the same structural-guidance variants.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain the same Pred-All and Oracle-Obj protocols, metrics, dataset splits, model configurations, and checkpoint selection. Training remains 20,000 iterations with batch size 8 and initial learning rate 0.0001.

E4.justification: The compositional-loss and DINO-guidance ablations, recall analysis, correspondence visualizations, and qualitative examples are retained. New red boxes in Figures A5–A7 highlight existing examples without adding analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and A1–A3 retain all numerical entries. For example, Pascal-Part-116 h-IoU remains 45.77 for Pred-All and 50.41 for Oracle-Obj. The underlying appendix qualitative examples and their findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, mathematical formulation, and Equations (1)–(16) are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: object-aware part cost aggregation, compositional loss, and DINO structural guidance, with the same claims about segmentation performance and generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of compositional loss and structural guidance remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the limitations concerning extremely fine-grained distinctions and the inability to distinguish separate part instances, together with the same proposed future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same implementation details, hyperparameters, eight A6000 GPUs, PyTorch 2.2, and code repository link. Removing 'anonymized' from the repository description does not change the supplied access information.

R1.justification: The same 83 cited works and research positioning are retained. Bibliography differences concern pagination and citation back-references, rather than added literature or revised relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgements, removes the repeated title and 'Supplementary Material' heading at the appendix opening, and removes 'anonymized' from Appendix B.1. The scientific prose and section sequence otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 4, and 5 receive typography or schematic revisions; Figure 4 removes DINO connections to class aggregation. Figures A5–A7 add red highlight boxes around existing examples. Bibliography and appendix content reflows, without new result displays.

improvement.justification: Figure 4 now depicts DINO routing consistently with Section 3.6's spatial-aggregation description, and Figures A5–A7 highlight the small-part differences discussed in the text. These provide limited improvements in explanatory clarity; the scientific evidence, conclusions, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
